diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 32–40 takes X={a} and H=<a^2>. The free rank-one reduced words are unique a^n, n in Z; multiplying by even powers partitions these into even H and odd Ha. Thus there are exactly two vertices, with base vertex H.

The generator edge rule Hg -> Hgx at line 40 gives the upper a-edge H -> Ha and lower a-edge Ha -> Ha^2=H. Both labels are a, not inverse labels. The right-multiplication transition is a permutation of these two cosets; each vertex has one outgoing and one incoming generator edge.

diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 42–44 gives backward label a^{-1} and right-product endpoints. The two forward edges produce H -> Ha -> H, endpoint Haa=Ha^2=H; the upper edge backward gives Ha -> H, endpoint Haa^{-1}=H. Native standalone PNG visibly has both distinct curved edges with the correct arrowheads, two circled vertices, two a labels, indegree=outdegree=1 at each vertex. The unlabelled incoming basepoint marker is not a graph edge. Closure is an explicit Ha-to-H curved segment, not --cycle.
